oracle.expected_behavior_note: Only the job posting is loaded. It says what the company needs (accessibility work beyond linting, having taken a complex interface through an audit, and the whole workspace to WCAG 2.2 AA); it holds no record of any audit she has been through. The answer must say plainly that it has no record of her audits and must not supply an auditor, a product, a conformance level or a date. In particular WCAG 2.2 AA is the hiring company's target, not a level she is known to have passed. It stays useful: the shape of a good answer for her to fill in (which product, internal or external auditor, the level and date, what the audit found, what she fixed, how she tested with assistive technology).

optional_facts.text: The posting requires accessibility work beyond linting: a complex interface taken through an audit.
The hiring company's own target is WCAG 2.2 AA for the whole workspace.

forbidden_claims.text: Supplies an audit, a product, an auditor, a level or a date as hers (the real ones are on a CV that is not loaded).
Presents the posting's WCAG 2.2 AA target as the level she passed.
Answers with the other candidate's facts (the backend profile: his employer, projects, numbers or the posting he applied to).

oracle.expected_role: assistant answering the candidate's private typed question: facts stated plainly to the candidate, or first-person wording the candidate can say
acceptable_inference: Offering wording such as 'The audit I took a product through was ...' for her to complete.

items.speaker: other
items.question: Before we get going, what's your understanding of what this team is actually responsible for?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The posting answers this plainly: the team is Ledger Core, and it owns three things: the double-entry ledger, the idempotency layer in front of every money-moving API, and the daily reconciliation between the company's books, processor reports and bank statements. The answer gives those three directly, in his voice, without hedging. It may add the team's size (9 engineers: 7 backend and 2 site reliability). Nothing about his own background is loaded, so none is added as fact.

required_facts.text: The double-entry ledger.
The idempotency layer in front of every money-moving API.
The daily reconciliation.

optional_facts.text: 9 engineers: 7 backend engineers and 2 site reliability engineers.
A Kafka backbone carries ledger events to settlement, risk and reporting.

forbidden_claims.text: Says he does not know what the team does, or only asks the interviewer to explain.
Adds responsibilities the posting does not give the team.
Adds his own employer or projects as fact, with no résumé loaded.
Answers with the other candidate's facts (the frontend profile: her employer, projects, numbers or the posting she applied to).

oracle.expected_role: the candidate answering the interviewer aloud, in the first person

items.speaker: user
items.question: quick one before the pairing bit: what's their collab layer built on, and how many people can be in one doc at the same time?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The posting answers this plainly: conflict-free editing runs on a CRDT layer, Yjs over WebSockets, in documents with up to 50 people editing at once. The answer gives both. The near miss is the 500-block document in the performance target, which is a document size and not a number of people. Nothing about her own experience with CRDTs is loaded, so none is claimed.

required_facts.text: A CRDT layer: Yjs over WebSockets.
Up to 50 people editing one document at once.

optional_facts.text: Having shipped real-time collaborative or multiplayer features is a requirement.

forbidden_claims.text: Gives the 500 of the performance target, or another number, as the number of people in a document.
Names another collaboration technology as theirs.
Says she has worked with Yjs or CRDTs, or names her employer, with no CV loaded.
Says the posting does not say.
Answers with the other candidate's facts (the backend profile: his employer, projects, numbers or the posting he applied to).

oracle.expected_role: assistant answering the candidate's private typed question: facts stated plainly to the candidate, or first-person wording the candidate can say
